description: RETURNS QUOTABLE PASSAGES (page-level snippets + citation URLs), matched by KEYWORD/term. PICK THIS to find a quote or textual evidence on a topic across the whole library. → If the modern word won't literally appear in historical texts, use search_concept (matches by meaning); to list which BOOKS cover a topic use search_library; to dig inside one known book use search_within_book; if the user named an author/work, get_book first (its AI summary is usually the right first read). Query tips: a distinctive term ("wax tablet") or the sentence you are looking for both work; matching is by word, and a page that prints your words together and in order ranks above one that scatters them. Each passage carries phrase_match (0-1, absolute, not relative to the other results): 1 means the page prints your whole query in order at one place, 0 means your words occur only apart; when every passage is under about 0.2 the library probably does not print that sentence, so try search_concept. It is absent for a one-word query and for a passage found by meaning alone. found_by says which lane found the page: "keyword", "semantic", or "both" (the strongest signal). Each snippet has a snippet_type — "translation"/"ocr" means it is a verbatim extract from the source text; "summary" means it is AI-generated description (do not quote those as the author's words). Response includes total_matches, returned, and offset for pagination. Cross-cultural tip: for pre-modern or non-Western topics, search source-tradition vocabulary rather than modern English terms — e.g. for seminal economy search "jing" or "bindu" or "istimnāʾ", not "semen retention"; for female homoeroticism search "tribade" or "sahq", not "lesbian". The corpus is indexed via period translations that use tradition-internal terminology.

author.description: Keep only passages by these authors, e.g. ["Ficino"] or ["della Porta", "Agrippa"]. Matches by name: every word you give must start a word of the book's author field.

diversity.description: Re-order the passages for spread. "author": at most one passage per author and per work in each ten, for a cross-author survey. "tradition": at most 2 per tradition family and per work. Default "off": passages come in relevance order. Nothing is dropped; later pages hold the rest.

exclude_authors.description: Drop passages by these authors, e.g. ["Agrippa"]. Use it to iterate a survey: run, see who dominates, exclude, run again.

exclude_languages.description: Exclude these languages, e.g. ["Latin", "French", "German", "English"] to surface non-Western sources.

lang.description: ISO code of the EDITION to read, e.g. "es". Default "en". Most books have only English — call get_book and read `editions`, or list_books with has_edition, to find the ones that do not. The response always states which edition it served.

language.description: Filter by a single original language

languages.description: Filter to any of these languages, e.g. ["Sanskrit", "Arabic", "Chinese"]. Use instead of language when targeting multiple traditions.

max_per_author.description: Hard cap on passages from one author; the rest are DROPPED (unlike diversity, which only re-orders). Set 1 for "N quotes from N different authors".

max_per_work.description: Hard cap on passages from one WORK (all printings and editions of it count together, via work_id), so seven printings of De occulta philosophia are one witness, not seven.

offset.description: Pagination offset (use with limit to page through total_matches; default 0)

query.description: A distinctive term ("harmony of the spheres", "active intellect") or the sentence you are looking for. A multi-word query matches pages printing ANY of its words, ranked so that pages printing them together come first (see phrase_match); wrap in "double quotes" to require the exact phrase.
